question: True or false: in a 2025 Turing test, people judged a chatbot to be the human more often than the real human?
answer: True. In five-minute three-way chats, each interrogator messaged a person and a machine at once, then picked the human. GPT-4.5, told to play a shy young adult fond of slang, was picked 73% of the time, so the real person only 27%. ELIZA, a 1966 program, was picked 23% of the time.
move: Past clumsiness is a poor guide to how easy a thing is to spot today.
trap: Recalling clumsy chatbots and assuming a person is easy to tell apart.
reference: Jones & Bergen, Large Language Models Pass the Turing Test, arXiv, 2025
